body.statement:
Assume, as an additional displayed premise, either the affirmative conclusion specified in \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\) or a separately proved sufficient compatibility package providing the same computable finite-library modulus and verifiable ledgers.  Then, for every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\) and rational \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\operatorname{CertGluePFL}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\) terminates and returns a replayable globally honest primal rule, a finite rational atomic dual certificate, and outward rational endpoints
\[
L_{\varepsilon}\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_{\varepsilon},
\qquad U_{\varepsilon}-L_{\varepsilon}\le\varepsilon.
\]
It also returns explicit total recursive bounds \(N_{\mathrm{glue}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{cut}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{Gauss}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), \(N_{\mathrm{LP}}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), and \(\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\), recorded in \(\mathsf C\).  The theorem is conditional and does not assert an affirmative answer to \(\text{oeq:effective-compatible-density}\).
body.justification: A convergence theorem without a finite stopping recurrence would not support certified statistical practice.
body.gap: Jones and Peet give an a priori integration error, Jungen, Djelassi, and Mitsos give conditional convergence for finite-dimensional semi-infinite programs, and Cousins and Vempala give randomized Gaussian-volume approximation; none certifies this function-valued minimax game with exact honesty and a matched atomic dual.
body.consumer: For the Job Corps assertion list, the output archives the exact observed-cell-to-\(\mathfrak G_0\) encoding, the simultaneous honest label rule, the primal and atomic-dual objects, and every outward integration and repair charge; this replayable certificate is required because a floating-point optimizer cannot establish global honesty on tied capacity, sign, or cross-quantile faces.
body.proof_tex:
\textbf{Technique: effective dovetailing of sound primal and dual semidecisions.}

This proof begins with the additional premise in the statement; it does not derive that premise from the standing assumptions.  The exact part of the affirmative effective-compatible-density conclusion needed here is a computable sequence \(\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)\downarrow0\) and enumerable finite records \(Q_j(K)\in\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) such that, for every \(K\in\mathcal C_\eta\), the record eventually produced for index \(j\) has a verifiable outward ledger satisfying
\[
\begin{split}
c\{Q_j(K)\}&\ge1-\eta-\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
r\{Q_j(K)\}&\le R_r(K)+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j),\\
\rho_{\mathrm{led}}\{Q_j(K)\}&\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j).
\end{split}
\tag{41}
\]
Here \(c(Q)\) is the infimum of semantic-label coverage and \(r(Q)\) is the supremum of separated diameter risk.  The premise includes finite certificates for canonical-section preservation, safety of every positive-weight candidate, collar discrepancy, translated tails, and refinement counts.  A separately proved sufficient compatibility package is admissible precisely when it supplies (41) with the same verifiability and computability properties.

At stage \(s\), enumerate the finitely many indices \(j\le s\), codes of records in \(\mathfrak F_{\mathfrak G,j}\) of length at most \(s\), rational incidence forests, semantic projections, atomic action probabilities, and integration and rounding precisions among the first \(s\) choices.  The checks in \(\text{def:weighted-error-ledger}\) return rational outward enclosures
\[
c^-_{Q,s}\le c(Q),
\qquad r(Q)\le r^+_{Q,s}.
\tag{42}
\]
A record is accepted only after every rational incidence, projection, protected-neighborhood, covariance, Gaussian-tail, quadrature, and rounding check needed for (42) has passed.  Thus acceptance uses no uncertified floating-point sign.

After intersecting the coverage enclosure with \([0,1]\), set
\[
\rho_{Q,s}=\max\{0,1-\eta-c^-_{Q,s}\},
\qquad q_{Q,s}=\frac{\rho_{Q,s}}{\eta+\rho_{Q,s}}.
\tag{43}
\]
Because \(0<\eta<1/2\) and \(0\le c^-_{Q,s}\le1\),
\[
0\le\rho_{Q,s}\le1-\eta<1,
\qquad \eta+\rho_{Q,s}>0.
\tag{44}
\]
Thus the division in (43) is valid, and (42)--(43) imply
\(c(Q)\ge1-\eta-\rho_{Q,s}\).  By \(\text{lem:exact-coverage-repair}\), the archived rule
\(Q^+=\operatorname{Repair}_{\eta,\rho_{Q,s}}(Q)\) is globally honest and
\[
M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
\le R_r(Q^+)
\le r^+_{Q,s}+Dq_{Q,s}.
\tag{45}
\]
Outward interval arithmetic produces a rational \(U_{Q,s}\) no smaller than the last expression in (45).

In parallel, enumerate the finite atomic dual records from \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), with rational weights and rational real-algebraic support encodings.  Membership in a finite union \(D_v\) and membership in \(H_r\) reduce to finitely many exact polynomial-sign, rational polyhedral, and convex quadratic-distance tests.  Refine each feasible record's Gaussian integrals until a rational lower endpoint \(l^-_{\nu,s}\) is obtained.  Every such endpoint is a valid lower certificate.  Put
\[
L_s=\max_{\nu\text{ processed by }s}l^-_{\nu,s},
\qquad
U_s=\min_{Q\text{ accepted by }s}U_{Q,s},
\tag{46}
\]
leaving an endpoint undefined if its finite collection is empty.  Weak duality and (45) imply, whenever both are defined,
\[
L_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\le U_s.
\tag{47}
\]

Each fixed stage terminates.  Its enumerated collections are finite, its geometry checks are finite exact rational or real-algebraic programs, and each requested Gaussian enclosure is obtained on a rational box by interval subdivision, with the complement bounded by an explicit Gaussian tail.  Accepted finite records carry moduli on the box, so the subdivision error tends to zero; the tail tends to zero as the box expands.  Every positive requested enclosure width is therefore reached after finitely many operations.

It remains to prove that the stopping test is eventually met.  By \(\text{thm:attainment-atomic-duality}\), there is \(K^*\in\mathcal C_\eta\) with
\[
R_r(K^*)=M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
\tag{48}
\]
Apply (41) to \(K^*\).  For any rational \(\zeta>0\), sufficiently fine outward evaluation of its finite record gives
\[
c^-_{Q_j(K^*),s}\ge c\{Q_j(K^*)\}-\zeta,
\qquad
r^+_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le r\{Q_j(K^*)\}+\zeta.
\tag{49}
\]
Equations (41), (43), and (49) imply
\[
\rho_{Q_j(K^*),s}\le\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta.
\tag{50}
\]
Combining (41), (45), and (48)--(50), and assigning at most another \(\zeta\) to the final outward rounding, gives
\[
U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
+D\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+2\zeta
+\frac{D\{\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta\}}
{\eta+\Omega_{\mathfrak G}(j)+\zeta}.
\tag{51}
\]
The denominator is positive by \(\eta>0\).  First increase \(j\), then decrease \(\zeta\); the right side tends to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The atomic-duality theorem also gives an enumerated increasing sequence of lower certificates converging to the same value.  Hence
\[
L_s\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r),
\qquad \limsup_{s\to\infty}U_s\le M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r).
\tag{52}
\]
Together with (47), (52) proves that some finite stage satisfies \(U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\).

For the cost receipt, let \(a_i(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the number of operations of type
\(i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\}\) at stage \(s\), and let \(b(\mathfrak G,s)\) be the largest bit length encountered there.  Define by primitive recursion
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_i(0)&=a_i(\mathfrak G,0),&
C_i(s+1)&=C_i(s)+a_i(\mathfrak G,s+1),\\
B(0)&=b(\mathfrak G,0),&
B(s+1)&=\max\{B(s),b(\mathfrak G,s+1)\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{53}
\]
Let
\[
s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
=\min\{s:L_s,U_s\text{ are defined and }U_s-L_s\le\varepsilon\}.
\tag{54}
\]
The test in (54) is rational, and (52) proves that its sequential search halts.  Therefore \(s_*\) is total recursive under the displayed conditional premise.  Set
\[
N_i(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)=C_i\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\},
\quad
i\in\{\mathrm{glue},\mathrm{cut},\mathrm{Gauss},\mathrm{LP}\},
\tag{55}
\]
\[
\operatorname{Bit}(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)
=B\{s_*(\mathfrak G,\varepsilon)\}.
\tag{56}
\]
Archive at stage \(s_*\) the repaired primal attaining the finite minimum and the atomic dual attaining the finite maximum in (46).  Equations (47), (54)--(56) give the asserted gap, exact honesty, termination, and five-part receipt.  All conclusions remain conditional on (41).
